content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text labels Luke 2:48-49 UNDERDETERMINED and reasons from the relation between 'thy father' and 'my Father's business,' so it invokes K-S2's treatment of a verse with two senses.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed reading 1: both clauses ('thy father' and 'my Father's business') stand as distinct senses and the verse is not open, against reading 2: the second clause qualifies the first, so the verse remains open/underdetermined.","why":"By treating the lowercase 'thy father' as qualified by the uppercase 'my Father's business' and still marking the verse UNDERDETERMINED, the judge makes a two-sense verse open, contrary to K-S2's requirement that both senses stand and it is not open."}
